# Quickstart — Your First Agent

Build an agent with tool access in 10 minutes.

## Prerequisites

- Completed the <a href="javascript:openLink('/terminal_client/quickstart')">Hello World quickstart</a>

## Step 1 of 4: Install the Shell Plugin

<div style="background: #f0f7ff; border-left: 4px solid #0066cc; padding: 12px 16px; margin: 16px 0; border-radius: 4px;">
<strong>Step 1 of 4 — Install the Shell Plugin</strong><br>
<div style="background: #e0e0e0; border-radius: 4px; height: 8px; margin-top: 8px;">
<div style="background: #0066cc; width: 25%; height: 100%; border-radius: 4px;"></div>
</div>
<span style="font-size: 12px; color: #666; margin-top: 4px; display: inline-block;">Current step: Install the Shell Plugin</span>
</div>

The shell plugin provides sandboxed shell and Python execution tools for your agents:

```bash
npm i -g @agent-smith/feat-shell
```

Register its features:

```bash
lm conf
```

## Step 2 of 4: Create Your Features Directory

<div style="background: #f0f7ff; border-left: 4px solid #0066cc; padding: 12px 16px; margin: 16px 0; border-radius: 4px;">
<strong>Step 2 of 4 — Create Your Features Directory</strong><br>
<div style="background: #e0e0e0; border-radius: 4px; height: 8px; margin-top: 8px;">
<div style="background: #0066cc; width: 50%; height: 100%; border-radius: 4px;"></div>
</div>
<span style="font-size: 12px; color: #666; margin-top: 4px; display: inline-block;">Current step: Create your features directory</span>
</div>

Create a directory structure for your custom features:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/my-agents/features/agents
```

Add this path to your config (`~/.config/agent-smith/config.yml`):

```yaml
backends:
  default: "llamacpp"
  llamacpp:
    type: "llamacpp"
    url: "http://localhost:8080/v1"

features:
  - ~/my-agents/features
```

Sync the config:

```bash
lm conf
```

> **Note**: `lm conf` syncs your YAML config file into the SQLite database. `lm update` scans your features directory for new agents, actions, and workflows. You'll use both commands at different times.

## Step 3 of 4: Create an Agent

<div style="background: #f0f7ff; border-left: 4px solid #0066cc; padding: 12px 16px; margin: 16px 0; border-radius: 4px;">
<strong>Step 3 of 4 — Create an Agent</strong><br>
<div style="background: #e0e0e0; border-radius: 4px; height: 8px; margin-top: 8px;">
<div style="background: #0066cc; width: 75%; height: 100%; border-radius: 4px;"></div>
</div>
<span style="font-size: 12px; color: #666; margin-top: 4px; display: inline-block;">Current step: Create an agent</span>
</div>

Create a YAML agent definition in your features directory. This agent will use the `shell` tool to execute commands:

```yaml
# ~/my-agents/features/agents/shell-demo.yml
description: A demo agent with shell access
prompt: |-
    {prompt}
model: qwen2.5
toolsList:
  - shell
```

> **Tip**: This minimal YAML uses default inference parameters. See <a href="javascript:openLink('/terminal_client/agents/overview')">Customizing Agents</a> for advanced options like `inferParams`, `variables`, and more.

## Step 4 of 4: Register and Run

<div style="background: #f0f7ff; border-left: 4px solid #0066cc; padding: 12px 16px; margin: 16px 0; border-radius: 4px;">
<strong>Step 4 of 4 — Register and Run</strong><br>
<div style="background: #e0e0e0; border-radius: 4px; height: 8px; margin-top: 8px;">
<div style="background: #0066cc; width: 100%; height: 100%; border-radius: 4px;"></div>
</div>
<span style="font-size: 12px; color: #666; margin-top: 4px; display: inline-block;">Current step: Register and run your agent</span>
</div>

Register your new agent:

```bash
lm update
```

This scans your features directory, parses the YAML definition, and registers the agent in the database.

Verify it was registered:

```bash
lm agent shell-demo
```

Run your agent:

```bash
lm shell-demo "List files in the current directory"
```

### Example Output

```
⚒️  Executing [shell-demo] shell { cmd: 'ls' }
README.md
package.json
src/

The current directory contains: README.md, package.json, src/
```
